pr_title: Fix build on OPENSSL_SYS_TANDEM and older POSIXes
pr_body:
This should hopefully fix not just the build on NONSTOP platform but also older POSIX systems.

It also allows for passing `-DOPENSSL_NO_LOCALE` as a workaround to `./Configure` command.

This is alternative to #18233

Fixes #18232

issue_context.title: regression in 3.0.3: strcasecmp_l is not working when using glibc 2.25 or older
issue_context.body:
Before glibc 2.26 (fix was in commit https://github.com/bminor/glibc/commit/7b037c095e31c2396d0a9b0e6356bc566ee4812f), the `strcasecmp_l` function was defined in two headers: `<string.h>` and `<strings.h>`.
However, the former was only defined if `_GNU_SOURCE` is used and the latter used the proper POSIX check.
If you include both headers in this order, the symbol will not get defined if `_POSIX_C_SOURCE >= 200809L` but `_GNU_SOURCE` is not defined.

We hit exactly this case, when compiling OpenSSL on Centos 7 (x64):
```
crypto/ctype.c:355:12: warning: implicit declaration of function 'strncasecmp_l' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
    return strncasecmp_l(s1, s2, n, (locale_t)ossl_c_locale());
```

To fix this issue, I'd propose either of the following solutions:
- Define `_GNU_SOURCE` in `ctype.c`, there are some files in libcrypto that already do this
- Replace the order of the includes to include `<strings.h>` before `<string.h>`. This is uglier, but also works.
comments: strings.h cannot be included before string.h on every platform, so the second suggestion would have negative consequences.
Could you please try the fixes in #18241?

> strings.h cannot be included before string.h on every platform, so the second suggestion would have negative consequences.

Really? I see we are including "e_os.h" which implicitly includes strings.h before string.h in multiple files.
I will try the latest set right now.
@t8m  Do you want me to remove #18233 at this stage?

> > strings.h cannot be included before string.h on every platform, so the second suggestion would have negative consequences.

It looks like my info was out of date. This was a problem but not at this point. I think it is only an issue if `_XOPEN_SOURCE` is not supplied or has a very old value. I can dig deeper if you want but it is working in the OpenSSL build.
